clue.text: Crown prince's tip after bad time in House

indicators.note: after puts the prince's tip at the end of the word
in places the bad-time pair inside the abbreviation for house

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill effects

indicators.note: the tip of a word here is its first letter

explanation.surface: A royal heir gets a bad-time warning while sitting in a legislative House.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crown' looks like a royal word next to 'prince', but it means the top of a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: The crown of a hill is its highest point, its summit.

clue.text: Quibbling resulting in damage to locks?

definitions.meaning: read literally, causing split ends in hair, the locks on one's head

explanation.surface: Pedantic argument is jokingly said to wreck someone's hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks' suggests doors and keys, but they are locks of hair; the question mark flags the literal reading of splitting hairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Making over-fine distinctions is the idiom splitting hairs, the very essence of quibbling.

clue.text: Bird with tail up, trapped in fine fabric screen

indicators.note: trapped in puts the altered bird inside the fabric word

parts.note: lace is a delicate openwork fabric

indicators.note: in a down clue the tail rises to the top, so the bird's last letter moves to its front

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A small bird, tail raised, gets caught in a delicate fabric screen.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the tail is at the bottom, so 'with tail up' shifts the bird's final letter to its top.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice is a criss-cross framework often used as a screen or trellis.

clue.text: Speed was satisfactory for going up river

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: met, as in met the requirements, means was satisfactory
the Po is the great river of northern Italy

explanation.surface: A boat's speed was judged adequate for travelling upstream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going up' turns MET into TEM; then add PO, the Italian river.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempo is the pace or rate at which something moves, especially music.

clue.text: Travel document father left around ship

indicators.note: around has the father and left pieces enclosing the ship abbreviation

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
port is the left side of a ship
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A dad has left his travel papers somewhere aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' is not departed but the nautical word for the left side of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport is the official document a traveller shows at borders.

clue.text: Intimidate a Georgian hymn-writer

parts.note: to cow is to intimidate or overawe
per means a, as in five pounds a head

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to bully a hymn-writer from Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Georgian' suggests the country or US state, but means the Georgian era of the British kings George I to IV. William Cowper wrote the Olney Hymns.
explanation.definitionFit: William Cowper, the 18th-century poet, co-wrote the Olney Hymns, including God Moves in a Mysterious Way.

clue.text: Relaxed about general being beheaded

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: being beheaded loses the first letter of the word for general

parts.note: usual means general or customary

explanation.surface: Someone stays relaxed about a general facing execution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like an army officer but is the adjective meaning customary.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual describes an informal, easygoing manner, synonymous with laid-back.

clue.text: Argumentative mathematicians at Cambridge?

parts.note: the word means people who argue, and also Cambridge students gaining first-class maths degrees

explanation.surface: Quarrelsome maths dons at a famous university.
explanation.walkthrough: At Cambridge University, students achieving first-class honours in mathematics are traditionally given this title; elsewhere it means people who squabble.
explanation.definitionFit: The word denotes both quarrelsome disputants and, at Cambridge, top-class mathematics graduates.

clue.text: In incident, help regularly is outstanding, we hear

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of help

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for outstanding is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: owed means still outstanding, as of a debt

explanation.surface: During some event, assistance repeatedly proves remarkable, or so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' suggests excellent, but means still owed, as a bill; 'regularly' takes E and P from 'help'.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is a single event or occurrence within a longer sequence.

clue.text: Necks of land in south one ponders over

indicators.note: in signals the south abbreviation is placed inside the musing phrase

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
to muse over something is to ponder it
STH is an abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Narrow land strips in the south are something a person mulls over.
explanation.walkthrough: South is abbreviated here to three letters rather than the usual single S; 'necks' is not anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: A neck of land is a narrow strip joining two larger landmasses, exactly an isthmus.

clue.text: A long universal farewell

parts.note: to be dying for something is to long for it
U is the film certificate meaning suitable for all, universal

explanation.surface: A lengthy goodbye addressed to everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective but is the verb, as in dying to see someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is a French-derived word of parting, meaning goodbye.

clue.text: Entirely new punt needed to travel round play area

indicators.note: round has the scrambled letters enclosing the play-area word
to travel suggests the letters moving about into a new order

parts.note: rec, short for recreation ground, is a play area

explanation.surface: A punt must journey around a playground in a way never seen before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To travel' shuffles PUNT NEEDED into UNPEDENTED, and 'round' puts it around REC, the British short form of recreation ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without precedent has never happened before, so it is entirely new.

clue.text: County set living in great opulence initially

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each word from set to opulence

explanation.surface: A county is portrayed as a place where a set of people live in luxury.
explanation.walkthrough: Sligo is a county in north-west Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Sligo is one of the counties of the Republic of Ireland, in Connacht.

clue.text: Where infants may be given scope to mature out West?

parts.note: play means scope or freedom of movement, as in giving a rope some play

indicators.note: out signals the West letter is taken away from the phrase

parts.note: to grow up is to mature

explanation.surface: A place where small children get the chance to develop, perhaps out in the West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' removes W from GROW UP, leaving GROUP; 'scope' is PLAY, as in leeway.
explanation.definitionFit: Preschool children may be given a place at a playgroup, an informal nursery session.

clue.text: Nautical device Europeans installed in seedy old bar

indicators.note: installed in puts the European pair inside the jumbled letters
seedy, meaning shabby or out of sorts, signals the letters are disordered

parts.note: E for European, twice for the plural

explanation.surface: Some Europeans set up a nautical gadget in a run-down old pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seedy' rearranges OLD BAR into LBOARD, and 'installed in' puts EE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A leeboard is a plank lowered on a sailing barge's side to reduce leeway, a piece of boat equipment.

clue.text: Primate phoned in striking article

indicators.note: in puts the telephoning word inside the word for striking

parts.note: workers out are on strike, so out means striking
rang means phoned
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A monkey has been telephoned in a newspaper piece about a strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' suggests impressive, but means on strike, OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: The orang-utan is a great ape, and apes belong to the primate order.

clue.text: Embarrassed look a flasher may get, on reflection?

definitions.text: a flasher may get, on reflection?

parts.note: red, as in red-faced, means embarrassed
to eye is to look at

explanation.surface: An indecent exposer, thinking it over, might earn a mortified glance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flasher' suggests an exhibitionist; here it is a camera flash, whose light reflecting off the retina makes pupils glow in photos.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera flash bouncing off the retina causes the glowing-pupil effect in photographs.

clue.text: Source of knitwear is real, if unusual

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters taken in an uncommon order

explanation.surface: A knitwear supplier is genuine, if a bit odd.
explanation.walkthrough: Fair Isle, in the Shetland Islands, gives its name to a patterned knitting style.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair Isle, a Shetland island, is where the multicoloured knitting pattern originated.

clue.text: International leader featured in giant painting

indicators.note: featured in puts the leading letter inside the giant word

parts.note: a titan is a giant

indicators.note: leader takes the first letter of international

explanation.surface: A global head of state appears in an enormous artwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' takes I from International, which 'featured in' puts inside TITAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A work by the Venetian master Titian is itself called a Titian, as one might say a Rembrandt.

clue.text: Leftist set-up encompassing soldiers' anguish

indicators.note: encompassing has the overturned leftist surround the soldiers
set up in a down clue means turned upward, read backwards

parts.note: Trot, short for Trotskyist, is a leftist
men means soldiers, the possessive adding no letters

explanation.surface: A left-wing plot embraces the troops' suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set-up' looks like a plot but reverses TROT into TORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Torment is intense suffering, mental or physical, much like anguish.

clue.text: Service area in West Brazil butchery

parts.note: Mass is a church service
Acre is a state in western Brazil, and also a unit of area

explanation.surface: A church service in a region of Brazil turns into slaughter.
explanation.walkthrough: ACRE works twice: a measure of area and a Brazilian state in the far west.
explanation.definitionFit: A massacre is wholesale slaughter, butchery of many people.

clue.text: Bottle needing can-opener these days

parts.note: the opener, or first letter, of can is C
these days is our age, the present time

explanation.surface: Opening a bottle these days seems to need a tin opener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' is British slang for nerve; 'can-opener' is read as the opening letter of 'can'.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, having bottle means having nerve or bravery.

clue.text: Cloth headgear raised in a film-making centre

indicators.note: in places the raised headgear inside the pair of other pieces

parts.note: LA, Los Angeles, is home to Hollywood

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a cap is headgear

explanation.surface: Fabric hats are held up in a Hollywood-style film centre.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'raised' reads the headgear from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpaca is a soft fabric woven from the wool of the South American animal.

clue.text: Abnormal, unlike full-time soldiers

definitions.meaning: describing militia or guerrilla fighters outside the standing professional army

explanation.surface: Part-time troops are described as odd.
explanation.walkthrough: Regular soldiers are the professional army; irregulars are militia or guerrillas.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses rest on not conforming to the regular pattern or the regular army.

clue.text: Lucky break for a parasitic worm!

definitions.meaning: a chance stroke of good luck

explanation.surface: Someone thinks catching a parasite counts as good luck.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a chance success and a parasitic flatworm infesting livers.

clue.text: Cast having good time

definitions.meaning: a brief period of carefree enjoyment

explanation.definitionFit: To fling is to throw, and a fling is a short spell of indulgent enjoyment.

clue.text: Salute short Cretan, say, at entrance to taverna

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a Cretan is an example of a Greek

indicators.note: entrance to takes the first letter of taverna

explanation.surface: A short islander welcomes visitors at a Greek tavern door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like height but trims GREEK to GREE; 'entrance to' adds the T of 'taverna'.
explanation.definitionFit: To salute someone is to acknowledge them with a gesture, a form of welcoming.

clue.text: He attacks while worker is framing canvas

indicators.note: framing has the while and worker words enclose the canvas word

parts.note: as can mean while, as in as I was walking
the ant is the crossword's stock worker
a sail is made of canvas

explanation.surface: An attacker strikes while a labourer stretches canvas in a frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canvas' suggests painting, but it is what a boat's sail is made of.
explanation.definitionFit: An assailant is a person who attacks another; the clue's he-who-attacks phrase is that agent noun.

clue.text: Laurel an unknown originally apostrophised in verse

parts.note: Stan Laurel was the thin half of the comedy duo Laurel and Hardy
in algebra, z is an unknown quantity

indicators.note: originally takes the first letter of apostrophised

explanation.surface: An obscure figure named Laurel was addressed in poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laurel' suggests the poet's wreath but is Stan Laurel.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza is a group of lines forming a unit of a poem.

clue.text: Intellectual, such as ambassador captured by tribe

parts.note: e.g. means for example, such as

indicators.note: captured by puts the ambassador inside the tribe

parts.note: Gad was one of the twelve tribes of Israel
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: An academic, an envoy for example, is seized by a tribe.
explanation.walkthrough: HE stands for His Excellency, an ambassador's title; Gad is a tribe of Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: Egghead is a jocular term for a bookish, highly intelligent person.
